title: ELECTION RESULTS
full_story:
Turnout in Clay County for yesterday’s primary was low with only 2,869 of the 9,175 voter casting ballots.  There are currently 315 outstanding Vote By Mail ballots and results will not be final until March 31st.

Clay County voters had 3 questions on their ballots in the first the Question was “Larkinsburg Township proposition to prohibit the sale of Alcohol” 40 people voted yes and 123 voted no.  For the “Clay County proposition to levy a special highway tax” 843 voted yes with 1,853 people voting against.  The “Clay County Federal Scholarship Tax Credit Advisory Referendum” 1,494 voted in favor and 1,166 voted against.

On the republican ballot there was a race for the County Board in District 8, Jonathan Piperakis has 115 votes compared to Rod Franklins 77 and John Baylers 51.  Clay County voters overwhelmingly voted for States Attorney Phillip Givens for 4th Circuit Judge.  Givens got 1,526 votes, and his nearest competitor Brenda Mathis had 305 votes.  For US Senator Clay County voters picked Don Tracy to fill the senate seat being vacated by Dick Durbin.  Clay County voters also overwhelmingly supported Darren Bailey for Governor with 91% of the vote.

On the Democratic Ballot voters picked Juliana Straton for the state senate seat being vacated by Dick Durbin, and Holly Kim as State Comptroller.

Republican voters in Illinois have once again chosen former state Sen. Darren Bailey as their candidate for governor, giving him a second chance to unseat incumbent Democrat JB Pritzker in November.  Bailey, was the party’s 2022 nominee, claimed victory last night in a four-way primary for the GOP nomination.  According to unofficial returns compiled by the Associated Press, Bailey had carried about 50% of the vote as about 8:35 p.m. when the race was called.  Speaking to a crowd of supporters at a Springfield hotel Tuesday night as his lead grew, Bailey immediately began calling for party unity.

title: NO BODY TO MURDER
full_story:
A play titled “No Body to Murder” will be held at Nostalgia Theater, formerly the Town Theater, in downtown Flora.  The play will be held on Friday, April 10th, and Saturday, April 11th, at 7 pm each night.  This fun whodunnit takes place on a stormy night and will have you laughing along and keep you guessing.  This is a stage performance, not a murder mystery event and there will be no audience participation.

The play is directed by Stacey Earleywine and is full of amazing local talent, who will blow you away with their acting abilities.  Although this play is not a musical, it is full of great songs in between scenes.

Grab a friend and enjoy an evening out with well-known community theater members Jeremy Kohn, Jim Earleywine, Matt Lovett, Jessica Muskopf, Linda Waller, Sarah Hager, and more.

Nostalgia Theater is currently being renovated and will serve as Clay County’s home for community theater.  Not only will you be able to catch some amazing live entertainment at Nostalgia, but the building is also for rent as a venue for upcoming events, such as parties, reunions, showers, and weddings.

Nostalgia Theater operates as a 501©3 non-profit and all proceeds from the Nostalgia play performances will be used to continue the renovation of the theater.  Make plans to attend this fun performance, support the hard work these actors have put into it, and see the beautiful Nostalgia Theater building as it is being brought back to life.

Tickets are $10 each.  Tickets are on sale Wednesday through Friday at Cuttin’ Up Hair Salon, next to Nostalgia Theater.  Tickets will also be available at the door.

title: REDUCED RATE LABS
full_story:
Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics will be hosting their popular “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” beginning April 15th through April 30th.  You may at any time pick up a voucher at the Clay County Hospital, or at the Flora, Louisville or Clay City Clinics during regular business hours.

The blood draws must be completed April 15th through April 30th.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday – Friday, 7 am – 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am -11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher. The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” April 15th through April 30th.

title: OCC MUSICAL
full_story:
Olney Central College Theater’s production of the musical Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat opens on Friday at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center.

The production marks the return of the beloved musical to the OCC stage for the first time in 18 years.  Known for its lively music and colorful storytelling, Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat retells the familiar biblical story of Joseph, his famous coat of many colors, and his journey from hardship to triumph.

This year’s production brings together a large community cast spanning generations.  Performers range in age from 15 to their mid-70s, and the show features a 50-member children’s choir, adding extra energy and excitement to the show.

While audiences will recognize the classic story and many of the well-known songs, this OCC Theater production also has a few surprises along the way.

The production is fun and accessible for audiences of all ages, making it a family-friendly night at the theater.

Performances will take place Friday and Saturday, and again on Thursday, March 26th, Friday, March 27th, and Saturday, March 28th at 7 pm and on Sunday, March 22nd and 29th at 2 pm, at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center on the Olney Central College campus.

Tickets are $14 for reserved seating and are available now at www.iecc.edu/occ/theater or by calling 618-395-7777, ext. 2408.

title: BROADCAST COMMUNICATION EVENT
full_story:
If you’ve ever thought about a career in radio, TV, or multimedia, Lake Land College has an event worth putting on your calendar.

The college’s Broadcast Communication Department is hosting an open house on Friday, March 20th from noon to 2 pm.  Lunch will be provided at noon, and the event follows the college’s Laker Visit Day.

This isn’t just a sit-down-and-listen kind of event.  Attendees will get hands-on time with professional audio and video equipment and a tour of the college’s very own student-run FM station, WLKL 89.9, The Max Alternative.  Additionally, you’ll have a chance to chat with faculty and current students about what the program entails.

Instructor and Director of Broadcast Operations Greg Powers says it’s a great fit whether you’re focused on a broadcasting career or just looking to pick up some solid multimedia skills along the way.

Students in the program can earn an associate degree which can lead straight to a job or transfer to a four-year university.  You would also have the option to choose from three different certificate programs.  The hands-on experience covers everything from anchoring newscasts and calling live sports to podcasting, digital editing, and working behind the scenes in a TV studio.

To register, head to www.lakelandcollege.edu/visit.  For more information, contact Greg Powers at [email protected] or 217-234-5335.

title: CARLYLE LAKE VOLUNTEER EVENT
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers, in partnership with the Carlyle Lake Education Habitat and Preservation (CLEHP) group and community volunteers, will host a volunteer workday Saturday to improve fish habitat and enhance fisheries at Carlyle Lake.

The event will begin at 8:00 am Saturday at the Allen Branch Boat Ramp located within Eldon Hazlet State Park.  During this workday, volunteers will help place habitat structures in the lake along with approximately 250 recycled Christmas trees.  Participants will assist with loading and transporting the materials for placement in designated areas of the lake.  Volunteers who have boats and are willing to assist with transporting and placing structures on the water are encouraged to participate.

Together, the recycled trees and artificial structures will form fish reef habitats throughout Carlyle Lake.  These habitats provide essential cover and spawning areas for fish, while also supporting the growth of algae and zooplankton that serve as important food sources for young fish.  Recycled Christmas trees offer an inexpensive and effective method for creating habitats that benefit a wide variety of fish species.

For more information, please contact the Carlyle Lake Project Office at (618) 594-2484 or email [email protected].

title: IDOR TAX ALERT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) is alerting taxpayers that changes announced by the United States Postal Service (USPS) regarding postmarks could impact tax filings in 2026.

While the USPS postmark will still show the date of the first automated processing operation, the postmark may no longer reflect the date when the piece of mail was dropped off at a local post office.  This change can directly impact time-sensitive documents such as tax returns and payments.

IDOR encourages those taxpayers who mail their returns and tax payments to do so earlier than they typically would to ensure they meet the Wednesday, April 15th filing deadline.

“Our goal is to help taxpayers avoid unnecessary stress and penalties, “explained IDOR Director David Harris.  “If returns are mailed, taxpayers should not wait until the last day, or they should request manual postmarks at the post office if they are mailing a return near the filing deadline.”

USPS will continue to apply manual local postmarks upon request at retail locations free of charge.  These manual postmarks will align with the date USPS first takes possession of the mail.

Harris stressed that electronic filing is the simplest and most convenient way to ensure tax documents and payments are received in a timely manner.

“The most reliable method to ensure IDOR receives a return or payment on time is to submit them electronically,” Harris said.  “Taxpayers may visit tax.illinois.gov for free electronic tax filing and payment options and use MyTax Illinois to file a return and make payments for free.”

Taxpayers who are not required by Illinois law to file or pay electronically may drop off returns or payments at an IDOR office.  IDOR staff will date stamp documents to provide accurate proof of receipt.

“Planning ahead is the best way taxpayers can protect themselves from late penalties,” Harris said.  “Allowing extra mailing time, obtaining a manual postmark or IDOR date stamp, or using electronic filing options can reduce delays and ensure returns and payments are received on time.”
